name: Tell Aswad barley with domestication traits
description: In Tell Aswad’s phase AW2, domestic-type, non-shattering forms constitute a substantial share of the identified barley spikelet bases. Wild-type remains still predominate.

impact.note: One site's barley remains with non-shattering forms; a new ability locally, on the line to Southwest Asian cereal farming.

date.label: Approximately 8200–7500 cal BCE (Middle PPNB, phase AW2)
date.basis: Douché and Willcox’s table 1 gives the approximate calendar interval of archaeological phase AW2.

events.statement: In Tell Aswad’s phase AW2, domestic-type, non-shattering forms constitute a substantial share of the identified barley spikelet bases. Wild-type remains still predominate.

evidence.supports: Using secure Pre-Pottery Neolithic B contexts and a revised stratigraphy, the authors report that domestic-type barley spikelet bases first form a substantial share in phase AW2. Table 1 dates AW2 to approximately 8200–7500 cal BCE.

events.caveats: The date refers to the phase yielding the remains. The revised study places the first substantial representation of this trait at Tell Aswad in AW2. The time and place where domestication began remain uncertain.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest phase with substantial representation of the domestication trait in the revised study of secure Tell Aswad contexts.

caveats: The date refers to the phase yielding the remains. The revised study places the first substantial representation of this trait at Tell Aswad in AW2. The time and place where domestication began remain uncertain.

research.note: Uses the 2018 secure-context reanalysis and revised phasing in place of the older estimate summarized by Zeder in 2011.
